newsitem.title: USA: Iowa county votes racetrack profits to schools.
newsitem.headline: Iowa county votes racetrack profits to schools.

text.p: Polk County, Iowa, supervisors Tuesday adopted a plan to share nearly two-thirds of their expected $16.8 million fiscal 1998 racetrack profits with local school districts, county spokesman Phil Roeder said.
The plan will divide 65 percent of the profits from the county-owned and partly bond-financed Prairie Meadows Race Track for public school infrastructure improvements, Roeder said.
While profits will fluctuate, the board has indicated that it wants to continue providing aid to the schools as long as Prairie Meadows continues to generate profits for Polk County, Roeder said.

Sixteen public school districts will receive allocations ranging from $2,000 for the smallest to $6.17 million for the Des Moines schools under the plan, which is based mostly on a per-capita formula.
The remaining 35 percent of the profits will be targeted to human services needs.

Supervisors are considering selling the now highly profitable race track, which has been appraised at $160 million. Prairie Meadows had been on the verge of bankruptcy until a massive turnaround sparked by the installation of slot machines in 1995.

Polk County has sought an opinion on the possible economic impact selling the track would have on the county. Supervisors also asked the state appeals board for an advisory opinion on the possible effect of receiving a profit twice the size of the county's annual budget.

Polk County had supported Prairie Meadows with $26.5 million of gaming revenue bonds in 1995 before the economic turnaround. It also sold $38.8 million of tax-exempt general obligation bonds in 1993 to sustain the facility.
Revenues for 1997 have been projected at $123.5 million.
